newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soybean output seen 37.1 mln tonnes by 2005.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean output seen 37.1 mln tonnes by 2005.

text.p: Brazilian soybean production could reach 37.1 million tonnes by the year 2005, a rise of 39 percent on the 26.7 million tonnes produced in 1997, said a member of the board of the Brazilian Vegetable Oils Industries Association (Abiove).

Acreage will increase by 2.4 million hectares mainly in the areas close to the new transport corridors, said Sergio Barroso in a copy of a speech delivered last week to the International Association of Seed Crushers in Budapest.
Total planted area is estimated at 13.9 million hectares against 11.5 million this year while yields should grow to 2.7 tonnes per hectare against 2.3 tonnes in 1996/97.
Soybean exports are seen at nine million tonnes and imports at two million tonnes in the year 2005.
Abiove has just revised its estimate for soybean exports this year to 8.5 million tonnes from a previous level of eight million tonnes. It puts imports at 1.5 million tonnes.
Crushings should grow to 27.5 million tonnes compared with a latest forecast of 18 million tonnes.
"The increased crush levels will significantly reduce the Brazilian industry's idle capacity," Barroso said in the speech.
Domestic soymeal and soyoil consumption are seen rising to eight million and 3.3 million tonnes, respectively, from expected levels of 5.5 million and 2.75 million tonnes in 1997.
"The big increase in domestic consumption of soymeal and soyoil signals a perspective of increased per capita consumption of animal proteins and oils in Brazil," Barroso said.

Soymeal exports are expected to reach 13.7 million tonnes from a current forecast of 8.9 million while soyoil sales overseas should total 1.9 million tonnes against an expected 850,000 tonnes this year.
